name: Chapel Street Church
tagline: An old stone church on a busy corner, keeping an open door and a long table since 1887.
office_hours: Church office open Tuesday to Friday, 9am – 3pm
footer_note: All are welcome. All means all.
bulletin_date: Sunday, September 27 · the 18th Sunday after Pentecost

bulletin.rubric: All stand as they are able.
Everyone is welcome to receive, or to come forward for a blessing.

bulletin.detail: Hymn 118 · Now Thank We All Our God

first_visit.title: Arrive
first_visit.body: Park on Linden Avenue or in our lot behind the hall. A greeter at the red doors will point you to a seat, the nursery, and the coffee.

first_visit.title: Worship
first_visit.body: About an hour of hymns, scripture, a twenty-minute sermon, and communion. Everything you need to follow along is printed in the bulletin.

first_visit.title: Stay
first_visit.body: Coffee and something baked in the hall afterward. No sign-up sheets, no pressure — just a chance to meet a few people.

faqs.question: What should I wear?
faqs.answer: Whatever you are comfortable in. You will see suits and you will see jeans, sometimes in the same pew.

faqs.question: Is there something for my children?
faqs.answer: A staffed nursery for under-threes runs through both services. Older children join Sunday School at 9:00 and come back in for communion.

faqs.question: Is the building accessible?
faqs.answer: Yes. There is a ramp at the Linden Avenue door, an accessible restroom off the hall, and large-print bulletins at the welcome table.

faqs.question: Do I have to be a member to take communion?
faqs.answer: No. Everyone is welcome at the table. If you would rather not receive, cross your arms and the priest will offer a blessing.

faqs.question: Can I just come and sit at the back?
faqs.answer: Of course. Plenty of people have started exactly there, and nobody will ask you to stand up and introduce yourself.

art_direction.identity: A parish church printed like its own prayer book: lime-washed paper canvas, warm stone panels, hymnal-black ink, vermilion used the way red rubrics are used in a liturgy book. Quiet, unhurried, welcoming — never a concert-lighting megachurch site.
art_direction.type: EB Garamond for every heading, set large with italic for the second phrase of a headline and small caps for labels; Instrument Sans for body copy and UI. Old-style numerals for times.
art_direction.color: One accent: vermilion (bg-primary / text-primary) for the primary button, rubric lines, and small ornaments only. Deep evening slate (bg-secondary) carries exactly one dark band — the first-visit section. Everything else is paper canvas, stone surface, card white, ink and muted text. Never add another color.
art_direction.signature: The order of worship — this Sunday's service printed like the bulletin card: small-caps parts, leader rules, the hymn and reading on the right, and red italic rubrics underneath. Keep it wherever the design evolves. The arched window shape frames every photograph.
art_direction.voice: Warm, plain and a little literary. Short sentences, concrete details (parking, coffee, how long it lasts). No exclamation marks, no churchy jargon without explanation, no 'vibrant community'.
